title: Safety Reviews on Airbnb: An Information Tale
eligible_reason: No main-text specification satisfies PROTOCOL Section 2. (1) Tables 2, 4, 5 (and A8) regress log occupancy / log ADR on lag_vicinity_sr_cumu_dummy (listing has at least one cumulative vicinity-safety review through t-1; absorbing, listing-specific first-VSR month) with listing FE and zip-by-month FE, but every column also includes a second staggered treatment regressor (lag_listing_sr_cumu_dummy) and seven to eight time-varying listing controls; Table 2 Panel B uses 12-month/6-month window treatments that switch off plus 'before-window' dummies. (2) Table 3 (PSM-matched listing pairs, AirbnbVSRDID / AirbnbLSRDID) regresses Y on treat_property, post and interaction with listing FE and city-by-month FE and no covariates, but the additive pair-level `post` indicator (equal to 1 for both the treated listing and its matched control after the pair's firstvsrmonth) is a time-varying regressor beyond the binary treatment; following the project precedent (mnsc.2023.01006, mnsc.2024.07298) this is recorded as NOT eligible as reported, borderline/near-miss: dropping `post` yields a canonical TWFE on the matched sample. Table 3 columns 3-4 and 7-8 add post-period bins (interactionl3 ... interactiong12) together with post-bin main effects (postl3 ... postg12) and no pre-period leads. (3) Tables 6-8 and A9-A10 are user-level xtpoisson pair-FE models (nonlinear, pair FE only, no calendar-time FE). (4) Table 9 is a nested-logit 2SLS demand model. The only canonical event studies (eventdd with hdfe absorb(fe_city_month airbnbpropertyid), leads(40) lags(40) accum, matched controls with event_time missing) are appendix Figures A10-A11 (listings) and the Poisson-free appendix Figure A14 uses pair FE. In addition the shipped data are CTGAN synthetic (readme: 'does not carry any real-world meaning'), so no published estimate can be reproduced from the package.
design_notes: Package SyntheticData_PaperCode (readme.txt + PaperCode/ + SyntheticData/). Code_part1_syn.ipynb (Python: Figures, counterfactual market-share/GBV tables from the nested-logit utilities) and Code_part2_syn.do (Stata: main-text Tables 1-9); Code_part3_syn.ipynb and Code_part4_syn.do produce appendix figures/tables. Panel: Airbnb listing x year-month, five US cities, 2015-2019 (AirDNA). Treatment of interest in Tables 2/4/5: lag_vicinity_sr_cumu_dummy (VSR = vicinity safety review; LSR = listing safety review is the second treatment). Table 3 matched DiD: AirbnbVSRDID_syn.csv columns airbnbpropertyid, reportingmonth, city_code, zipcode, log_occupancy_rate, log_adr, treat_property, post, interaction, firstvsrmonth, pair_index; fe_city_month = group(city_code Month). Synthetic file shows 45 distinct firstvsrmonth values (2015-11 .. 2019-07) among treated listings, 1,566 pairs, 56 months 2015-05..2019-12, but CTGAN output is internally inconsistent (interaction != treat_property*post in 11,557 of 147,576 rows; 483 listings carry more than one firstvsrmonth), so counts describe marginals only. Table 2 regressions use fe_zip_month + airbnbpropertyid with vce(cluster airbnbpropertyid) keepsingletons; Table 3 reghdfe calls specify no vce option (conventional SEs) and treat_property is collinear with the listing FE. Appendix Figures A10/A11: eventdd log_occupancy_rate / log_adr, timevar(event_time) [= month_diff for treated listings, missing for matched controls], method(hdfe, absorb(fe_city_month airbnbpropertyid)) leads(40) lags(40) accum; this is an unstacked event study with listing FE and city-by-month FE and no covariates, eligible by design but appendix-only and on synthetic data.
n_eligible_specs_note: 0 main-text specs. 4 appendix event studies (Figures A10-A11: occupancy and ADR for VSR and LSR matched samples) qualify by design but are appendix-only and the data are synthetic; 8 Table 3 columns are near-misses because of the additive pair-level post indicator.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: 45 distinct firstvsrmonth (2015-11..2019-07) and 45 distinct firstlsrmonth among treated listings in the synthetic matched files; monthly adoption. Real counts unknown (synthetic marginals).
never_treated_note: Matched control listings never receive a VSR/LSR by construction (treat_property = 0); in the Table 2 full panel, listings with no safety review are untreated throughout.

data_files: SyntheticData/AirbnbAll_syn.csv (962 MB, listing-month, 2,866,238 rows; Tables 1, 2, 4, 5, A3, A8)
SyntheticData/AirbnbVSRDID_syn.csv (147,576 rows) and AirbnbLSRDID_syn.csv (161,427 rows): matched listing pairs for Table 3 and Figures A10-A11
SyntheticData/VSRusersDID_MRes_syn.csv, VSRusersDID_ResProp_syn.csv, LSRusersDID_MRes_syn.csv, LSRusersDID_ResProp_syn.csv (user-level matched pairs, Tables 6-8)
SyntheticData/AirbnbEH_syn.csv (391 MB; Table 9 demand model), zip_rank_panel_syn.csv, VSR_text_syn.csv, LSR_text_syn.csv

All files generated with CTGAN (SDV 1.23.0) on 10-50% subsamples; readme: 'Please do not interpret the numbers'. Original sources: AirDNA (Airbnb, VRBO), STR hotel data, BTS, Zillow ZHVI, city crime records, Census.
software_notes: Stata (reghdfe, xtpoisson, eventdd, ivreghdfe, outreg2) for all regressions; Python notebooks for figures and counterfactual tables.
priority_note: Main-text designs ineligible (controls / second treatment / pair-level post indicator / Poisson). The matched-pair Table 3 and appendix Figures A10-A11 would be eligible on the real data only if the lead accepts the matched event study (appendix) or drops the `post` regressor; real data are confidential AirDNA/STR data, package is synthetic.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text; abstract truncated in frame). Full-text flags: 'difference-in-differences', 'staggered', cites Roth et al. 2023; no CSA/BJS/SA code anywhere in the package. The mapping of code blocks to table numbers follows the '//table N' comments in Code_part2_syn.do. Two judgement calls for the lead: (1) whether a pair-level `post` main effect disqualifies the matched-pair TWFE (recorded as not eligible, near-miss, following precedent); (2) appendix eventdd event studies are eligible by design but appendix-only.
